# odyssey-041 review (9.193–280)

Two passes, by hand. `t` untouched (checked: the units' `t` are identical before and after, and joined they equal the packet's 88 lines; 45 units; `p` on 193, 216, 231, 252, 256, 259, 272 as in the packet). Scansion flags in the packet: none, so nothing scanned or added to a note. `gloss.json` did not exist at review time, so the part of pass 2 that checks parses against the lines is still to do.

Severity: high = wrong sense or wrong text; medium = a false statement in a note or `about`; low = imprecise, unsupported, or a wording or consistency point.

Considered and refused:
- 209 as "cup of wine to twenty of water" being too strong a dilution to be meant: it is what the Greek says, and the note already calls it very heavy.
- ἀτάρ at 196 rendered "also" in `i`: "and yet" is in `l`; "also" is acceptable prose for the sense 'and moreover'.
- 9.253 vs 3.72: the note says "the same as 3.72–74"; Murray prints ἦ τι here against ἤ τι there, and commas differ. Same words, same sense; left, since the note is about the English being shared.
- πόρεν from "πόρω" (201): a lexicon head-word for an aorist-only verb; fine for a note.
- The "ancient commentators" on ἕρσαι (220) and "usual explanation" for Φοῖβος (200) are attributed, hedged and general; left.

Every unit was read word by word (case relations, tense, mood, particles) against `l`, and `l` against `i` for sense and force; the rest agree. The house rows in new-renderings.md are all applied as written: ποτιδόρπιον at 234 and 249; ὄβριμον at 233 and 241; ἐυεργέος/-α at 202 and 279 ("well-made"); ἠλίβατον "towering" with the note that the meaning is unknown; θυρεός "door-stone" against πέτρη "rock"; ἀκηράσιον "unmixed" tied in the note to 209; ἐπιτιμήτωρ "avenger"; ξείνιος; φέριστε "best of men"; ἐπιειμένον "clothed in great might"; the 272 and 258 formulas. Older rows checked: θυμὸς ἀγήνωρ "manly"/"proud", ἐρίηρες "trusty", τετυγμένα "wrought"/"well-wrought", ἄγριος "savage", ταμίη "housekeeper", ἀμφίπολοι "attendants", μηκάδες αἶγες, ὣς ἔφαθ’ "So he spoke". Nothing arrived as a remembered phrase; `i` was rebuilt from the grammar where checked (209, 212, 224–227, 246–249).

Quotation marks. Outer speech: Odysseus' tale opened “ at 9.2 (odyssey-039), and this part neither opens nor closes it, correctly; odyssey-040 ends inside it and this part runs on into 042 with no ” (the validator's unbalanced-marks warning does not fire, since only “ ” are counted). Inner speeches, single marks, as in odyssey-018 and 040: ‘ at 252 (mark "The Cyclops asks", p) closed ’ at 255; ‘ at 259 ("Odysseus answers the Cyclops", p) closed ’ at 271; ‘ at 273 ("The Cyclops answers") closed ’ at 280. Units between (253–254, 260–271 middle units) carry none, correct; 250, 256, 258 and 272 (narration) carry none. Every `mark` is on the first unit of its speech.

Decision on the merged 9.252 unit (two ;-questions in one unit): accepted. The convention would end the unit at each `;`, and odyssey-009 has 3.71 as two units. But the split units would have to open with ‘ while the published `l` has none, and `validate_odyssey.py` check 6 requires a repeated unit's `l` and `i` to be identical to the published ones, so the split would fail the gate. One unit of one line, with both questions in the published wording, does no harm to the reader. A line added to QUESTIONS.md asks whether the check should ignore quotation marks. 9.253–255 does not trip the check (ἦ against ἤ in the first word) and closes with ’ instead of the published ”.

## Left for the caller
- new-renderings.md, row for πρόγονοι · μέτασσαι · ἕρσαι, says "μέτασσαι occurs only here"; the unit note no longer does. Before the rows are copied into conventions.md the phrase should read "μέτασσαι is a rare word".
- Glosser: ᾖα here is the noun (known-forms entry has both readings; fine). μένομεν at 232 is an imperfect without augment, φέρτεροι a comparative, ἧος = ἕως, θυρεόν etc. as in the notes.

Judgements on the doubtful items:
- τ (broadened, ἦ τ’ at 228): accepted. The published entry covers τ’ only as connective, "epic τε" of a standing fact (which is what τοί τ’ at 253 is) and the question-τε; none of them covers ἦ τ’ ἂν … ἦεν, where τε strengthens ἦ. The added reading and its example are true of the line.
- τοὺς (broadened, 193): accepted. The published entry has ’them’ and the relative only; τοὺς ἄλλους … ἑταίρους is the pronoun standing with a noun ’the others’, the same use the published τὰ entry already records ("with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’"). A gloss of ’them’ alone would leave the reader with a pronoun and no construction.
- ναῖον ’flow’: kept. The vessels cannot ’dwell’ in whey; the reading with the dative ὀρῷ, ’were awash with whey’, is the traditional one, the entry now says it is a different verb from ναίω ’dwell’ and that the sense is the traditional one from context.

Considered and refused:
- δοίη (228, known entry "(purpose)"): the clause is καὶ εἴ … δοίη inside the ὄφρα purpose clause, so the parenthesis is not false; parse (aor. opt. 3 sg.) and sense cover the use. No broadening.
- κακὸν (253), κατὰ … πρῆξιν (253), ἤ … ἦ (279) and ἦ … ἦ (253), πὰρ + dat. (193), τι at 253 and 266, ἐπεὶ, ὅτε πίνοιεν (208): each is already covered by a reading in the published entry (checked in full). No broadening.
- τοῖς (222), φέρον and ἔχον (212, 196: impf. 1 sg.), ἐρυθρόν (masc. acc.), ἃ (250: possessive, τὰ ἃ ἔργα), αὖθ (220: = αὖτε ’again’, not αὖθι ’here’): the broadenings are true of the lines and were needed; unchanged.
- αὐτὸν at 205 (glossed ’him(self)’, the wine): the entry is not wrong as a parse; left.
- Entries with no change needed (checked case by case): the other 138 novel entries and 8 broadenings.
- Not done: `new-renderings.md` and `units.json` untouched by this pass.

Glossary pass counts: 16 entries changed (14 novel, 2 broadened): 0 high, 5 medium, 11 low; 2 broadenings judged sound and kept (τ, τοὺς), 1 doubtful sense kept (ναῖον).
